   215	    /// The menu arms, answered from `validateUserInterfaceItem`'s default
   216	    /// case; nil for any other action.
   217	    func validateAudioAction(_ action: Selector) -> Bool? {
   218	        switch action {
   219	        case #selector(normalizeClips(_:)):
   220	            // Load-bearing: without it Clip ▸ Normalize falls through to the
   221	            // closing `return true` and is live on a selection it could only
   222	            // beep at.
   223	            //
   224	            // It asks the command's own question of the MEMOIZED snapshot, not
   225	            // of the plan: a validator runs on every menu open, and
   226	            // `ReelProject.plan` decodes JSON on every access. The plan is
   227	            // still the honest answer to "does this clip make a sound", and
   228	            // `AudioNormalize.read` asks it — a clip enabled here but with no
   229	            // audio segment is reported under `skipped` rather than silently
   230	            // dropped, which is the right side to be wrong on.
   231	            //
   232	            // `AudioNormalize.canOffer` and not `InspectorTab.hasAudio`: a
   233	            // nest carrying anything audible has audio properties of its own,
   234	            // so `hasAudio` says yes about the one clip `read` can ONLY refuse
   235	            // (the plan flattens a nest, so the clip has no segment of its
   236	            // own). The Audio pane's button asks the same function through
   237	            // `AudioPane.normalizable`, which is what keeps a greyed button
   238	            // and a live menu item from disagreeing about one selection.
   239	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot else { return false }
   240	            return selectedClips.contains { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }
   241	        case #selector(enhanceVoice(_:)):
   242	            // Normalize's question, for Normalize's reasons (AU-60): the
   243	            // button asks it through `AudioPane.normalizable`.
   244	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot else { return false }
   245	            return selectedClips.contains { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }
   246	        case #selector(matchAudio(_:)):
   247	            // Two clips Normalize could measure (AU-121): one the reference.
   248	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot else { return false }
   249	            return selectedClips.filter { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }.count >= 2
   250	        case #selector(synchronizeAudio(_:)):
   251	            // Two clips that could play sound, asked of the snapshot for the
   252	            // reason above; `read` and `plan` may still refuse, by name.
   253	            guard let snapshot = document?.editedProject.snapshot else { return false }
   254	            return AudioSync.canOffer(selectedClips, in: snapshot)
   255	        default:
   256	            return nil
   257	        }
   258	    }

     3	/// The Synchronizing Audio sheet (road map "audio-sync-2", AS-4; spec §11
     4	/// SY-22): up while `AudioSync.plan` runs on a background queue, so the
     5	/// window never beach-balls on a long take.
     6	///
     7	/// `AudioSync.read` has already run on the main thread (it reads the
     8	/// document); the sheet takes its `Input` — values only, safe to hand to
     9	/// another thread — and runs the pure `plan` off main. While the sheet is
    10	/// attached every editor action validates false
    11	/// (`EditorViewController.validateUserInterfaceItem`), Synchronize Audio
    12	/// included, which is the bargain Reverse and Consolidate strike. When the
    13	/// plan comes back the sheet keeps it and dismisses itself; `finished` is
    14	/// called once, on the main queue's next turn after `viewDidDisappear`, so a
    15	/// Weak match sheet it brings up finds the window free. Cancel
    16	/// dismisses at once and the late plan is dropped: nothing moves.
    17	///
    18	/// **The dev hold** (`-RCDevSyncHold <seconds>`, dev tools only): the run
    19	/// waits that long before `plan`, so a proof can reach the sheet (S25, S26).
    20	final class AudioSyncSheetController: NSViewController {
    21	    /// The dev-only launch default that holds the run (SY-22).
    22	    static let devHoldKey = "RCDevSyncHold"
    23	
    24	    private let input: AudioSync.Input
    25	    private let finished: (AudioSync.Plan) -> Void
    26	
    27	    private let bar = NSProgressIndicator()
    28	    private let statusLabel = NSTextField(wrappingLabelWithString: "")
    29	    /// Set in `loadView`; implicitly unwrapped for exactly that reason
    30	    /// (app/CLAUDE.md).
    31	    private var cancelButton: NSButton!
    32	    private var hiddenButton: NSButton!
    33	
    34	    private var didStart = false
    35	    private var cancelled = false
    36	    private var answered = false
    37	    private var plan: AudioSync.Plan?
    38	
    39	    init(input: AudioSync.Input, finished: @escaping (AudioSync.Plan) -> Void) {
    40	        self.input = input
    41	        self.finished = finished
    42	        super.init(nibName: nil, bundle: nil)
    43	    }
    44	
    45	    @available(*, unavailable)
    46	    required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
    47	        fatalError("AudioSyncSheetController does not support NSCoder")
    48	    }
    49	
    50	    override func loadView() {
    51	        styleSheetProgressBar(bar, indeterminate: true)
    52	
    53	        styleSheetStatusLabel(statusLabel)
    54	        statusLabel.stringValue = "Matching the sound of \(input.readings.count) clips…"
    55	
    56	        let content = makeProgressStack([bar, statusLabel])
    57	
    58	        cancelButton = StickerButton(
    59	            title: "Cancel", style: .secondary, target: self, action: #selector(cancelClicked(_:)))
    60	        hiddenButton = StickerButton(title: "Apply", style: .primary, target: nil, action: nil)
    61	        hideReturnTarget(hiddenButton)
    62	
    63	        view = makeSheetView(
    64	            title: "Synchronizing Audio",
    65	            hint: "Nothing moves until the match is found; Cancel leaves everything as it is.",
    66	            content: content, buttonRow: makeButtonRow(cancel: cancelButton, apply: hiddenButton))
    67	    }
    68	
    69	    override func viewDidAppear() {
    70	        super.viewDidAppear()
    71	        guard !didStart else { return }
    72	        didStart = true
    73	        bar.startAnimation(nil)
    74	        let input = self.input
    75	        var hold = 0.0
    76	        #if FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS
    77	        hold = UserDefaults.standard.double(forKey: Self.devHoldKey)
    78	        #endif
    79	        DispatchQueue.global(qos: .userInitiated).async { [weak self] in
    80	            if hold > 0 { Thread.sleep(forTimeInterval: hold) }

    83	                guard let self, !self.cancelled else { return }
    84	                self.plan = plan
    85	                self.dismiss(self)
    86	            }
    87	        }
    88	    }
    89	
    90	    /// The one hand-back: once, with the plan, and never after Cancel. On
    91	    /// the next turn of the main queue, because while this runs the window
    92	    /// still reports this sheet as attached, and a Weak match sheet asked for
    93	    /// now would find the window taken (measured: S24 got a beep, no sheet).
    94	    override func viewDidDisappear() {
    95	        super.viewDidDisappear()
    96	        bar.stopAnimation(nil)
    97	        guard !answered, !cancelled, let plan else { return }
    98	        answered = true
    99	        let finished = self.finished
   100	        DispatchQueue.main.async { finished(plan) }
   101	    }
   102	
   103	    @objc private func cancelClicked(_ sender: Any?) {
   104	        guard !cancelled, plan == nil else { return }
   105	        cancelled = true
   106	        dismiss(self)
   107	    }
   108	}
        // UI path `enhance_voice` names. No key equivalent, for Normalize's

        menu.addItem(item("Enhance Voice", #selector(EditorViewController.enhanceVoice(_:))))

3	     3	/// Where Synchronize Audio looks and what it chooses (road map
4	     4	/// "audio-sync-2", AS-3; spec §11 SY-13, SY-14, SY-17, SY-18): the clips'
5	     5	/// played windows, the order of the two searches, the choice among a
6	     6	/// search's candidates and its tier, the candidate moves the answer reports,
7	     7	/// and the refusal that names them.
8	     8	///
9	     9	/// Pure, as `AudioSync.plan` is: two readings' features on their timeline
10	    10	/// grids in, a lag or a refusal out. The arithmetic of one search is
11	    11	/// `AudioSyncMatch.search`'s. A tier chosen here is only a candidate: `plan`
12	    12	/// keeps it only when GCC-PHAT on the samples finds a clear peak at it (the
13	    13	/// waveform gate, SY-29), and words the refusal when it does not
14	    14	/// (`incoherent`, `unconfirmed`).
15	    15	///
16	    16	/// **The played windows first** (SY-13, reversing AS-1's whole files): what
17	    17	/// the user trimmed each clip to is evidence of what they mean to line up,
18	    18	/// and the owner's files share a second, unrelated stretch that wins any
19	    19	/// whole-file search. The whole files are searched only when the played
20	    20	/// windows chose nothing and either window is a strict part of its file.
21	    21	extension AudioSync {
22	    22	
23	    23	    /// Which stretches a match was found in.
24	    24	    enum Search: String {
25	    25	        case played, whole
26	    26	    }
27	    27	
28	    28	    /// Which rule chose it (SY-14): `.confidence` is the CONFIDENT tier,
29	    29	    /// `.placement` the WEAK one, never applied silently (SY-18).
30	    30	    enum ChosenBy: String {
31	    31	        case confidence, placement
32	    32	    }
33	    33	
34	    34	    /// One candidate as the move it would make: its lag in ticks, the
35	    35	    /// frame-snapped delta, and its z.
36	    36	    struct CandidateMove: Equatable {
37	    37	        let offset: Ticks
38	    38	        let delta: Ticks
39	    39	        let confidence: Double
40	    40	    }
41	    41	
42	    42	    /// A chosen match: its lag in frames (anchor minus mover, file-relative,
43	    43	    /// on the timeline grid, refined), its z, where and how it was found,
44	    44	    /// what it correlated (SY-17), and the candidates the answer lists.
45	    45	    struct Found: Equatable {
46	    46	        let lag: Double
47	    47	        let confidence: Double
48	    48	        let search: Search
49	    49	        let chosenBy: ChosenBy
50	    50	        let matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn

52	    52	    }

61	    61	    /// The frames of a file (`frames` of them, on its timeline grid) that a
62	    62	    /// clip spanning `[start, end)` with its tick 0 at `zero` plays:
63	    63	    /// `[⌊(start − zero)/frameTicks⌋, ⌈(end − zero)/frameTicks⌉)`, clamped to
64	    64	    /// the file.
65	    65	    static func playedWindow(start: Ticks, end: Ticks, zero: Ticks, frames: Int) -> Range<Int> {
66	    66	        let step = Double(SyncFeatures.frameTicks)
67	    67	        let lower = Int((Double(start - zero) / step).rounded(.down))
68	    68	        let upper = Int((Double(end - zero) / step).rounded(.up))

74	    74	
75	    75	    /// The best candidate when it is confident on its own — z at least
76	    76	    /// `confidentZ` and `confidentMargin` above the second, or no second —
77	    77	    /// else the peak near the mover's placement when its z is at least

80	    80	        -> (AudioSyncMatch.Candidate, ChosenBy)? {

82	    82	           result.candidates.count < 2
83	    83	            || best.z - result.candidates[1].z >= AudioSyncMatch.confidentMargin {

176	   176	    static func refusal(anchor: UInt32, mover: UInt32, ran: [(Search, [CandidateMove])])

514	    13	    /// SY-32's region: `overlap` (anchor timeline frames) ×128, in anchor
515	    14	    /// timeline samples, when it holds at most W = `maximumRegionSamples /
516	    15	    /// hop` frames; else the W frames whose features agree most along
517	    16	    /// `line`. Frame f scores `Σ_k A[f, k]·M[m(f), k]`, A and M the features
518	    17	    /// `standardised` as the match was (over the speech frames when it
519	    18	    /// matched on speech), `m(f) = f − round((c + ρ·128f)/128)`, and 0 when
520	    19	    /// f or m(f) lies outside its file. The start s in `[lo, hi − W]` with
521	    20	    /// the greatest summed score wins; the centred start `⌊(lo + hi)/2⌋ −
522	    21	    /// ⌊W/2⌋` is the first candidate, replaced only by a strictly greater
523	    22	    /// sum or an equal one nearer it.
524	    23	    static func refinementRegion(
525	    24	        overlap: Range<Int>, anchorFrames: [Float], moverFrames: [Float], anchorSpeech: [Bool]?,
526	    25	        moverSpeech: [Bool]?, matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn, line: AudioSyncPHAT.Line
527	    26	    ) -> Range<Int> {
528	    27	        let hop = SyncFeatures.hop
529	    28	        let span = AudioSyncPHAT.maximumRegionSamples / hop
530	    29	        let lo = overlap.lowerBound
531	    30	        let hi = overlap.upperBound
532	    31	        guard overlap.count > span else { return (lo * hop)..<(hi * hop) }
533	    32	
534	    33	        let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
535	    34	        let onSpeech = matchedOn == .speech
536	    35	        let a = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(anchorFrames, speech: onSpeech ? anchorSpeech : nil)
537	    36	        let m = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(moverFrames, speech: onSpeech ? moverSpeech : nil)

539	    38	        let moverCount = m.count / width
540	    39	
541	    40	        // prefix[i] = Σ score over the overlap's first i frames.
542	    41	        var prefix = [Double](repeating: 0, count: overlap.count + 1)
543	    42	        a.withUnsafeBufferPointer { anchor in
544	    43	            m.withUnsafeBufferPointer { mover in
545	    44	                for (index, f) in overlap.enumerated() {

550	    49	                    if f >= 0, f < anchorCount, g >= 0, g < moverCount {

552	    51	                        let y = g * width
553	    52	                        for k in 0..<width { score += Double(anchor[x + k]) * Double(mover[y + k]) }

24	    24	/// (SY-17, frame k = source frame round(k·speed)), so a sound at timeline
25	    25	/// frame `f` plays at `zero + f·9600`; its samples are read at `t·speed`
26	    26	/// where they are used (SY-20). A mover whose sound at frame `m` is the
27	    27	/// anchor's at `m + lag` lines up when its zero becomes `zeroA + lag·9600`:
28	    28	/// `delta = zeroA − zeroN + lag·9600`, snapped to the frame grid (SY-4),
29	    29	/// because the model stores no sub-frame time.
30	    30	///
31	    31	/// **Drift and the refinement** (SY-6, SY-20, SY-21, SY-29). Over the overlap
32	    32	/// the coarse delta gives, the lag is fitted as a line, `lag(a) = c + ρ·a` (a
33	    33	/// an anchor timeline sample, 75 ticks each, c in samples); not measured, the
34	    34	/// line is the coarse lag. PHAT along it over the 30 s of the overlap whose
35	    35	/// features agree most (SY-32) — the files' overlap at the lag when that played
36	    36	/// overlap is under 2 s — shifts c by a clear peak's sub-sample shift. **The
37	    37	/// waveform gate** (SY-29): a match of either tier stands only on that clear
38	    38	/// peak; a peak that is not clear refuses the command (`incoherent`), and so
39	    39	/// does a refinement that cannot run (`unconfirmed`) unless neither reading
40	    40	/// carries samples at all, when the features' tier stands. Corrected
41	    41	/// (SY-8), the mover's speed becomes `s' = s·(1 − ρ)` and, since `set_speed`
42	    42	/// keeps its start S and in point I, source tick μ plays at `S + δ + (μ −
43	    43	/// I)/s'` — on the anchor's line everywhere when `δ = snapToFrame(round(zeroA
44	    44	/// + 75·c/(1 − ρ) − S + I/s'))` (`correctedDelta`). Left uncorrected, it is
45	    45	/// placed by the line's value at the overlap's centre aMid, `delta =
46	    46	/// snapToFrame(zeroA − zeroN + round((c + ρ·aMid)·75))`; not measured, by
47	    47	/// the (refined) lag. Snapping leaves one constant offset of at most half a
48	    48	/// frame.
49	    49	///
50	    50	/// **The head trim** (SY-16, the owner's choice): a mover that would start
51	    51	/// before 0 loses the excess off its head by a `trim_start` between the
52	    52	/// `set_speed` and the `move_clip`, so it starts at 0 and what remains plays
53	    53	/// in sync. **What it refuses rather than lets the core decide** (SY-4):
54	    54	/// `move_clip` clamps the earliest clip at 0, and on an overlap within the
55	    55	/// overlap rule it ADDS a cross dissolve instead of refusing — so a mover
56	    56	/// that would land on another clip of its own track is refused here, by
57	    57	/// name — on the FINAL span, after any change of speed or trim (SY-10).
58	    58	enum AudioSync {
59	    59	
60	    60	    // MARK: - Vocabulary
61	    61	
62	    62	    /// One reason the command will not run: about a clip ("clip N: …") or
63	    63	    /// about the selection as a whole (the reason alone).
64	    64	    struct Problem: Equatable {
65	    65	        let clip: UInt32?
66	    66	        let reason: String
67	    67	
68	    68	        var description: String {
69	    69	            guard let clip = clip else { return reason }
70	    70	            return "clip \(clip): \(reason)"
71	    71	        }
72	    72	    }
73	    73	
74	    74	    /// Another top-level clip on a reading's track, as the span it occupies.
75	    75	    struct Neighbour: Equatable {
76	    76	        let clip: UInt32
77	    77	        let start: Ticks
78	    78	        let end: Ticks
79	    79	    }
80	    80	
81	    81	    /// One clip that can be matched: where it sits, where its file's tick 0
82	    82	    /// plays, whether it has pictures (the anchor rule, SY-2), its file's
83	    83	    /// samples and sync features, and the clips it shares its track with.
84	    84	    struct Reading: Equatable {
85	    85	        let clip: UInt32
86	    86	        let media: UInt32
87	    87	        let trackIndex: Int
88	    88	        let start: Ticks
89	    89	        let end: Ticks
90	    90	        let zero: Ticks
91	    91	        let hasVideo: Bool
92	    92	        /// Its file's 8 kHz samples (`cache/sync/<id>.pcm`) on the SOURCE grid.
93	    93	        let samples: [Int16]
94	    94	        /// Its file's `SyncFeatures` frames on the SOURCE grid, frame-major.
95	    95	        let features: [Float]
96	    96	        /// Which of those frames are speech (SY-17), one per frame on the
97	    97	        /// SOURCE grid; nil when the voice model cannot be used.
98	    98	        let speech: [Bool]?
99	    99	        let neighbours: [Neighbour]
100	   100	        /// The clip's playback rate, within SY-9's band.
101	   101	        let speed: Double
102	   102	        /// Its first audio segment's in point, in source ticks.
103	   103	        let sourceIn: Ticks
104	   104	    }
105	   105	
106	   106	    /// Everything a run reads, taken off the document once.
107	   107	    struct Input {
108	   108	        let readings: [Reading]
109	   109	        let problems: [Problem]
110	   110	        /// The anchor the caller named, or nil for SY-2's rule.
111	   111	        let anchor: UInt32?
112	   112	        let fps: Fps
113	   113	    }
114	   114	
115	   115	    /// One mover's answer: its lag in ticks (refined, at the overlap's
116	   116	    /// centre), the coarse lag and the refinement (SY-20), the frame-snapped
117	   117	    /// move, where it lands, how sure the match was and how it was found,
118	   118	    /// what drift it measured, its speed, duration and correction after the
119	   119	    /// command, and the head it lost to start at 0 (SY-16).
120	   120	    struct Synced: Equatable {
121	   121	        let clip: UInt32
122	   122	        let media: UInt32
123	   123	        let lag: Ticks
124	   124	        /// The coarse match's lag in ticks, before the refinement.
125	   125	        let coarseLag: Ticks
126	   126	        /// The PHAT refinement over the overlap; nil when none ran.
127	   127	        let refinement: AudioSyncPHAT.Refinement?
128	   128	        let delta: Ticks
129	   129	        let start: Ticks
130	   130	        /// The chosen lag's z-score (SY-12).
131	   131	        let confidence: Double
132	   132	        let search: Search
133	   133	        let chosenBy: ChosenBy
134	   134	        let matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn
135	   135	        let candidates: [CandidateMove]
136	   136	        let drift: AudioSyncMatch.DriftAnswer
137	   137	        let speed: Double
138	   138	        let duration: Ticks
139	   139	        let correction: Correction
140	   140	        let trimmed: Ticks
141	   141	    }
142	   142	
143	   143	    enum Plan {
144	   144	        case refused([Problem])
145	   145	        case planned(anchor: UInt32, synced: [Synced], ops: [ReelOp])
146	   146	    }
147	   147	
148	   148	    // MARK: - Offering it
149	   149	
150	   150	    /// Whether the command can be offered: at least two selected clips pass
151	   151	    /// `AudioNormalize.canOffer` (sound, and not a nest). A cheap pre-check
152	   152	    /// of the snapshot, never the plan — `read` may still refuse.
153	   153	    static func canOffer(_ clips: [ClipSnapshot], in snapshot: ProjectSnapshot) -> Bool {
154	   154	        clips.filter { AudioNormalize.canOffer($0, in: snapshot) }.count >= 2
155	   155	    }
156	   156	
157	   157	    // MARK: - Reading
158	   158	
159	   159	    /// Reads the edited project's snapshot, plan, sync features and samples
160	   160	    /// and (with the voice model) speech probabilities for `clips` (nil:
161	   161	    /// the document's selection). nil only when the plan cannot be read; a
162	   162	    /// clip that cannot be matched is a `Problem`.
163	   163	    static func read(from document: ProjectDocument, clips: [UInt32]?, anchor: UInt32?)
164	   164	        -> Input? {
165	   165	        guard let plan = document.editedProject.plan else { return nil }
166	   166	        let snapshot = document.editedProject.snapshot
167	   167	
168	   168	        var audio: [UInt32: [PlanSegment]] = [:]
169	   169	        for track in plan.audioTracks {
170	   170	            for segment in track.segments where segment.duration > 0 {
171	   171	                audio[segment.clip, default: []].append(segment)
172	   172	            }
173	   173	        }
174	   174	        var pictured: Set<UInt32> = []
175	   175	        for track in plan.videoTracks {
176	   176	            for segment in track.segments where segment.duration > 0 {
177	   177	                pictured.insert(segment.clip)
178	   178	            }
179	   179	        }
180	   180	
181	   181	        var samplesByMedia: [UInt32: [Int16]] = [:]
182	   182	        var featuresByMedia: [UInt32: [Float]] = [:]
183	   183	        var speechByMedia: [UInt32: [Float]] = [:]
184	   184	        let voice = SileroVAD.isAvailable
185	   185	        var readings: [Reading] = []
186	   186	        var problems: [Problem] = []
187	   187	        var seen: Set<UInt32> = []
188	   188	        for id in clips ?? document.selection.sorted() where seen.insert(id).inserted {
189	   189	            guard let clip = snapshot.clip(id) else {
190	   190	                problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: "is not a clip in this project."))
191	   191	                continue
192	   192	            }
193	   193	            if case .nest = clip.source {
194	   194	                problems.append(
195	   195	                    Problem(
196	   196	                        clip: id,
197	   197	                        reason: "is a nest, and a nest has no sound of its own to match: the "
198	   198	                            + "waveform cache is per media file and the clips inside a nest "
199	   199	                            + "each have their own. Open it (⌘↓) and synchronize the clips "
200	   200	                            + "inside."))
201	   201	                continue
202	   202	            }
203	   203	            // A ramp's rate changes over the clip, and the drift line reads
204	   204	            // one (spec §11 SR-20 (e)); the map is the snapshot's handle's.
205	   205	            if document.editedProject.sourceMap(id)?.ramped == true {
206	   206	                problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: AudioSync.ramped))
207	   207	                continue
208	   208	            }
209	   209	            guard let segments = audio[id]?.sorted(by: { $0.start < $1.start }),
210	   210	                  let first = segments.first
211	   211	            else {
212	   212	                problems.append(
213	   213	                    Problem(
214	   214	                        clip: id,
215	   215	                        reason: "plays no sound in this timeline, so there is nothing to line "
216	   216	                            + "it up by. A still, a clip whose media has no audio track and a "
217	   217	                            + "clip with audio switched off all read this way."))
218	   218	                continue
219	   219	            }
220	   220	            if clip.speed != 1 || segments.contains(where: { $0.isTimeScaled }) {
221	   221	                let scaled = segments.first { $0.isTimeScaled } ?? first
222	   222	                let rate = clip.speed != 1
223	   223	                    ? clip.speed : Double(scaled.sourceDuration) / Double(max(scaled.duration, 1))
224	   224	                // At speed 1 a time-scaled segment is a stretch the clip's
225	   225	                // speed does not say, so neither `zero` nor `set_speed` can
226	   226	                // read it: refused, as AS-1 did (SY-9).
227	   227	                if let problem = rateProblem(rate) ?? (clip.speed == 1 ? stretched(rate) : nil) {
228	   228	                    problems.append(Problem(clip: id, reason: problem))
229	   229	                    continue
230	   230	                }
231	   231	            }
232	   232	            if case .media(_, _, true) = clip.source {
233	   233	                problems.append(
234	   234	                    Problem(
235	   235	                        clip: id,
236	   236	                        reason: "plays reversed; Synchronize Audio lines up clips playing "
237	   237	                            + "forwards."))
238	   238	                continue
239	   239	            }
240	   240	            let cached = featuresByMedia[first.media] ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
241	   241	                MediaImporter.loadSyncFeatures(for: first.media, in: $0)
242	   242	            }
243	   243	            let probabilities = !voice ? nil : speechByMedia[first.media]
244	   244	                ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
245	   245	                    MediaImporter.loadSpeech(for: first.media, in: $0)
246	   246	                }
247	   247	            let pcm = samplesByMedia[first.media] ?? document.cacheDirectory.flatMap {
248	   248	                MediaImporter.loadSyncSamples(for: first.media, in: $0)
249	   249	            }
250	   250	            // The samples are the features' own: a count that disagrees is a
251	   251	            // pass not finished, read as not written.
252	   252	            let written = cached.flatMap { features in
253	   253	                pcm.flatMap {
254	   254	                    SyncFeatures.frameCount(samples: $0.count)
255	   255	                        == features.count / SyncFeatures.coefficients ? $0 : nil
256	   256	                }
257	   257	            }
258	   258	            guard let features = cached, let samples = written, !voice || probabilities != nil
259	   259	            else {
260	   260	                // The waveform can be on the timeline while the features
261	   261	                // and speech that land after it are not: say which.
262	   262	                let missing = written == nil
263	   263	                    ? " for Synchronize Audio — its sound features have not been written yet."
264	   264	                    : " for Synchronize Audio — its speech has not been detected yet."
265	   265	                problems.append(
266	   266	                    Problem(
267	   267	                        clip: id,
268	   268	                        reason: "is still being analysed" + missing + " Try again in a moment."))
269	   269	                continue
270	   270	            }
271	   271	            featuresByMedia[first.media] = features
272	   272	            samplesByMedia[first.media] = samples
273	   273	            if let probabilities { speechByMedia[first.media] = probabilities }
274	   274	            let frames = features.count / SyncFeatures.coefficients
275	   275	            guard frames >= AudioSyncMatch.minimumStretchFrames else {
276	   276	                let seconds = String(
277	   277	                    format: "%g",
278	   278	                    Double(Ticks(AudioSyncMatch.minimumStretchFrames) * SyncFeatures.frameTicks)
279	   279	                        / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
280	   280	                problems.append(
281	   281	                    Problem(
282	   282	                        clip: id,
283	   283	                        reason: "is too short to match: its file holds under \(seconds) s of "
284	   284	                            + "sound."))
285	   285	                continue
286	   286	            }
287	   287	            let neighbours = snapshot.clips
288	   288	                .filter { $0.track == clip.track && $0.id != id }
289	   289	                .map { Neighbour(clip: $0.id, start: $0.start, end: $0.start + $0.duration) }
290	   290	            readings.append(
291	   291	                Reading(
292	   292	                    clip: id, media: first.media,
293	   293	                    trackIndex: snapshot.tracks.firstIndex { $0.id == clip.track } ?? 0,
294	   294	                    start: clip.start, end: clip.start + clip.duration,
295	   295	                    zero: first.start - Ticks((Double(first.sourceIn) / clip.speed).rounded()),
296	   296	                    hasVideo: pictured.contains(id), samples: samples, features: features,
297	   297	                    speech: probabilities.map { AudioSyncMatch.speechMask($0, frames: frames) },
298	   298	                    neighbours: neighbours,
299	   299	                    speed: clip.speed, sourceIn: first.sourceIn))
300	   300	        }
301	   301	        return Input(
302	   302	            readings: readings, problems: problems, anchor: anchor, fps: snapshot.canvas.fps)
303	   303	    }
304	   304	
305	   305	    // MARK: - The anchor (SY-2)
306	   306	
307	   307	    /// The named reading; else, among the readings with pictures (all of them
308	   308	    /// when none has), the earliest start, then the rearmost track, then the
309	   309	    /// lowest id.
310	   310	    static func chooseAnchor(_ readings: [Reading], named: UInt32?) -> Reading? {
311	   311	        if let named = named { return readings.first { $0.clip == named } }
312	   312	        let pictured = readings.filter { $0.hasVideo }
313	   313	        let pool = pictured.isEmpty ? readings : pictured
314	   314	        return pool.min { a, b in
315	   315	            if a.start != b.start { return a.start < b.start }
316	   316	            if a.trackIndex != b.trackIndex { return a.trackIndex < b.trackIndex }
317	   317	            return a.clip < b.clip
318	   318	        }
319	   319	    }
320	   320	
321	   321	    // MARK: - Planning (SY-1, SY-4, SY-6..SY-10, SY-12..SY-16)
322	   322	
323	   323	    /// The ops, or every reason there are none. All or nothing: one problem
324	   324	    /// anywhere refuses the whole command.
325	   325	    static func plan(_ input: Input) -> Plan {
326	   326	        guard input.problems.isEmpty else { return .refused(input.problems) }
327	   327	        let readings = input.readings
328	   328	        guard readings.count >= 2 else {
329	   329	            return .refused([
330	   330	                Problem(clip: nil, reason: "Synchronize Audio needs at least two clips with sound.")
331	   331	            ])
332	   332	        }
333	   333	        guard let anchor = chooseAnchor(readings, named: input.anchor) else {
334	   334	            return .refused([
335	   335	                Problem(
336	   336	                    clip: input.anchor,
337	   337	                    reason: "is not one of the clips being synchronized, so it cannot be the "
338	   338	                        + "anchor.")
339	   339	            ])
340	   340	        }
341	   341	
342	   342	        var problems: [Problem] = []
343	   343	        var byTrack: [Int: [UInt32]] = [:]
344	   344	        for reading in readings { byTrack[reading.trackIndex, default: []].append(reading.clip) }
345	   345	        for index in byTrack.keys.sorted() {
346	   346	            guard let ids = byTrack[index], ids.count > 1 else { continue }
347	   347	            let names = ids.map { "clip \($0)" }.joined(separator: " and ")
348	   348	            problems.append(
349	   349	                Problem(
350	   350	                    clip: nil,
351	   351	                    reason: "\(names) are on one track; Synchronize Audio lines up clips on "
352	   352	                        + "different tracks."))
353	   353	        }
354	   354	
355	   355	        // A file with no sound cannot be matched; the problem is the silent
356	   356	        // clip's own, so a silent anchor is named once, not on every mover.
357	   357	        let silent = "has no sound to line up by."
358	   358	        let anchorSilent = AudioSyncMatch.isSilent(anchor.features)
359	   359	        if anchorSilent { problems.append(Problem(clip: anchor.clip, reason: silent)) }
360	   360	        let anchorFrames = AudioSyncMatch.resampledFrames(anchor.features, speed: anchor.speed)
361	   361	        let anchorSpeech = anchor.speech.map {
362	   362	            AudioSyncMatch.resampledMask($0, speed: anchor.speed)
363	   363	        }
364	   364	
365	   365	        let hop = Double(SyncFeatures.hop)
366	   366	        let sample = Double(AudioSyncPHAT.sampleTicks)
367	   367	        // SY-22: one setup for every refinement this plan makes.
368	   368	        let fft = AudioSyncPHAT.FFT(log2n: AudioSyncPHAT.planLog2n)
369	   369	        var synced: [Synced] = []
370	   370	        var ops: [ReelOp] = []
371	   371	        for mover in readings where mover.clip != anchor.clip {
372	   372	            guard !AudioSyncMatch.isSilent(mover.features) else {
373	   373	                problems.append(Problem(clip: mover.clip, reason: silent))
374	   374	                continue
375	   375	            }
376	   376	            if anchorSilent { continue }
377	   377	            let moverFrames = AudioSyncMatch.resampledFrames(mover.features, speed: mover.speed)
378	   378	            let moverSpeech = mover.speech.map {
379	   379	                AudioSyncMatch.resampledMask($0, speed: mover.speed)
380	   380	            }
381	   381	            let found: Found
382	   382	            switch find(
383	   383	                anchor: anchor, anchorFrames: anchorFrames, anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech,
384	   384	                mover: mover, moverFrames: moverFrames, moverSpeech: moverSpeech, fps: input.fps)
385	   385	            {
386	   386	            case .refused(let problem):
387	   387	                problems.append(problem)
388	   388	                continue
389	   389	            case .found(let answer):
390	   390	                found = answer
391	   391	            }
392	   392	            let lagTicks = Ticks((found.lag * Double(SyncFeatures.frameTicks)).rounded())
393	   393	            let coarse = ReelTime.snapToFrame(anchor.zero - mover.zero + lagTicks, fps: input.fps)
394	   394	            let lower = frameIndex(max(anchor.start, mover.start + coarse) - anchor.zero)
395	   395	            let upper = frameIndex(min(anchor.end, mover.end + coarse) - anchor.zero)
396	   396	            let window = max(0, lower)..<max(0, lower, upper)
397	   397	            var drift = AudioSyncMatch.drift(
398	   398	                anchor: anchorFrames, mover: moverFrames, anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech,
399	   399	                moverSpeech: moverSpeech, anchorSamples: anchor.samples,
400	   400	                moverSamples: mover.samples, anchorSpeed: anchor.speed, moverSpeed: mover.speed,
401	   401	                lag: found.lag, overlap: window, fft: fft)
402	   402	            // SY-20: PHAT along the line over 30 s of the overlap (SY-32); under
403	   403	            // 2 s played, over the files' overlap at the lag instead (SY-29).
404	   404	            var line = AudioSyncPHAT.Line(intercept: found.lag * hop, rate: 0)
405	   405	            if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
406	   406	                line = AudioSyncPHAT.Line(intercept: fit.intercept, rate: fit.rate)
407	   407	            }
408	   408	            let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
409	   409	            let played = refinementRegion(
410	   410	                overlap: window, anchorFrames: anchorFrames, moverFrames: moverFrames,
411	   411	                anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech, moverSpeech: moverSpeech, matchedOn: found.matchedOn,
412	   412	                line: line)
413	   413	            let reach = played.count >= AudioSyncPHAT.minimumRegionSamples
414	   414	                ? played
415	   415	                : refinementRegion(
416	   416	                    overlap: filesOverlap(
417	   417	                        lag: found.lag, anchorFrames: anchorFrames.count / width,
418	   418	                        moverFrames: moverFrames.count / width),
419	   419	                    anchorFrames: anchorFrames, moverFrames: moverFrames,
420	   420	                    anchorSpeech: anchorSpeech, moverSpeech: moverSpeech,
421	   421	                    matchedOn: found.matchedOn, line: line)
422	   422	            let refinement = AudioSyncPHAT.refine(
423	   423	                anchor: anchor.samples, anchorSpeed: anchor.speed, mover: mover.samples,
424	   424	                moverSpeed: mover.speed, line: line, region: reach, fft: fft)
425	   425	            // SY-29, the waveform gate: either tier stands only on a clear
426	   426	            // peak; a refinement that could not run refuses too, unless
427	   427	            // neither reading carries samples at all.
428	   428	            if let refinement, !refinement.clear {
429	   429	                problems.append(
430	   430	                    Problem(
431	   431	                        clip: nil,
432	   432	                        reason: incoherent(
433	   433	                            anchor: anchor.clip, mover: mover.clip, delta: coarse,
434	   434	                            confidence: found.confidence, refinement: refinement)))
435	   435	                continue
436	   436	            }
437	   437	            if refinement == nil, !(anchor.samples.isEmpty && mover.samples.isEmpty) {
438	   438	                problems.append(
439	   439	                    Problem(
440	   440	                        clip: nil,
441	   441	                        reason: unconfirmed(
442	   442	                            anchor: anchor.clip, mover: mover.clip, delta: coarse,
443	   443	                            confidence: found.confidence)))
444	   444	                continue
445	   445	            }
446	   446	            var refinedTicks = lagTicks
447	   447	            var delta = coarse
448	   448	            if let refinement, refinement.clear {
449	   449	                if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
450	   450	                    drift = .measured(
451	   451	                        AudioSyncMatch.Drift(
452	   452	                            ppm: fit.ppm, milliseconds: fit.milliseconds, rate: fit.rate,
453	   453	                            intercept: fit.intercept + refinement.shift,
454	   454	                            errorMilliseconds: fit.errorMilliseconds, windows: fit.windows,
455	   455	                            on: fit.on))
456	   456	                } else {
457	   457	                    refinedTicks = Ticks(((found.lag * hop + refinement.shift) * sample).rounded())
458	   458	                    delta = ReelTime.snapToFrame(
459	   459	                        anchor.zero - mover.zero + refinedTicks, fps: input.fps)
460	   460	                }
461	   461	            }
462	   462	            let correction = Self.correction(for: drift, speed: mover.speed)
463	   463	            var newSpeed: Double?
464	   464	            if case .measured(let fit) = drift {
465	   465	                let centre = Double(window.lowerBound + window.upperBound) / 2 * hop
466	   466	                let line = Ticks(((fit.intercept + fit.rate * centre) * sample).rounded())

470	   470	                    newSpeed = speed

472	   472	                        anchor: anchor, mover: mover, drift: fit, speed: speed, fps: input.fps)
473	   473	                }
474	   474	            }
475	   475	            let duration = mover.end - mover.start
476	   476	            let newDuration = newSpeed.map {
477	   477	                durationAtSpeed(duration, from: mover.speed, to: $0, fps: input.fps)
478	   478	            } ?? duration

480	   480	            let excess = max(0, -(mover.start + delta))

484	   484	                let seconds = Double(excess) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond)

493	   493	            let grown = excess > 0 && newDuration > duration
494	   494	            let overlapStart = max(anchor.start, start)
495	   495	            let overlapEnd = min(anchor.end, end)
496	   496	            guard overlapStart < overlapEnd else {
497	   497	                problems.append(
498	   498	                    Problem(
499	   499	                        clip: mover.clip,
500	   500	                        reason: "once lined up it would not play at any moment clip "
501	   501	                            + "\(anchor.clip) plays."))
502	   502	                continue
503	   503	            }
504	   504	            if delta != 0 || newDuration != duration,
505	   505	               let hit = mover.neighbours.first(where: {
506	   506	                   (start < $0.end && $0.start < end)
507	   507	                       || (grown && mover.start < $0.end && $0.start < mover.start + newDuration)
508	   508	               }) {
509	   509	                problems.append(
510	   510	                    Problem(
511	   511	                        clip: mover.clip, reason: "would overlap clip \(hit.clip) on its track."))
512	   512	                continue
513	   513	            }
514	   514	            synced.append(
515	   515	                Synced(
516	   516	                    clip: mover.clip, media: mover.media, lag: refinedTicks,
517	   517	                    coarseLag: lagTicks, refinement: refinement, delta: delta,
518	   518	                    start: start, confidence: found.confidence, search: found.search,
519	   519	                    chosenBy: found.chosenBy, matchedOn: found.matchedOn,
520	   520	                    candidates: found.candidates, drift: drift,
521	   521	                    speed: newSpeed ?? mover.speed, duration: newDuration - excess,
522	   522	                    correction: correction, trimmed: excess))
523	   523	            ops += Self.ops(
524	   524	                clip: mover.clip, delta: delta, from: mover.speed, to: newSpeed,
525	   525	                duration: duration, newDuration: newDuration,
526	   526	                trimTo: excess > 0 ? mover.start + excess : nil)
527	   527	        }
528	   528	        guard problems.isEmpty else { return .refused(problems) }
529	   529	        return .planned(anchor: anchor.clip, synced: synced, ops: ops)
530	   530	    }

532	   532	    /// The anchor timeline frame holding `ticks` after its zero: `⌊ticks /
533	   533	    /// frameTicks⌋`.
534	   534	    private static func frameIndex(_ ticks: Ticks) -> Int {
535	   535	        let step = SyncFeatures.frameTicks
536	   536	        let quotient = ticks / step
537	   537	        return Int(ticks % step < 0 ? quotient - 1 : quotient)

540	   540	    /// SY-29's fallback region: the anchor timeline frames where the two
541	   541	    /// files (`anchorFrames` and `moverFrames` frames on their timeline
542	   542	    /// grids) overlap at `lag`, rounded outward — `[max(0, ⌊lag⌋), min(anchorFrames,
543	   543	    /// moverFrames + ⌈lag⌉))` — so every lag a search can score holds at
544	   544	    /// least `minimumOverlapFrames` (a sample read past a file's end is 0).
545	   545	    private static func filesOverlap(lag: Double, anchorFrames: Int, moverFrames: Int)
546	   546	        -> Range<Int> {
547	   547	        let lo = max(0, Int(lag.rounded(.down)))
548	   548	        let hi = max(lo, min(anchorFrames, moverFrames + Int(lag.rounded(.up))))

18	    18	/// and the owner's files share a second, unrelated stretch that wins any

29	    29	    /// `.placement` the WEAK one, never applied silently (SY-18).

31	    31	        case confidence, placement
32	    32	    }

40	    40	    }

61	    61	    /// The frames of a file (`frames` of them, on its timeline grid) that a

64	    64	    /// the file.

66	    66	        let step = Double(SyncFeatures.frameTicks)

68	    68	        let upper = Int((Double(end - zero) / step).rounded(.up))

170	   170	    /// "no matching sound found between clip A and clip N: in the played
171	   171	    /// windows, moving clip N by +0.77 s (confidence 4.31) or −12.40 s (3.90);
172	   172	    /// in the whole files, …. A match applies on its own at …. Either counts
173	   173	    /// only when the two waveforms line up there (…)." — every search that ran
174	   174	    /// with its candidates, and the rule printed from its constants; "…: too

176	   176	    static func refusal(anchor: UInt32, mover: UInt32, ran: [(Search, [CandidateMove])])
177	   177	        -> String {
178	   178	        let head = "no matching sound found between clip \(anchor) and clip \(mover)"
179	   179	        let named = ran.filter { !$0.1.isEmpty }
180	   180	        guard !named.isEmpty else { return head + ": too little room to compare their sound." }
181	   181	        func seconds(_ delta: Ticks) -> String {
182	   182	            String(format: "%+.2f", Double(delta) / Double(ReelTime.perSecond))
183	   183	                .replacingOccurrences(of: "-", with: "−") + " s"
184	   184	        }

186	   186	            let place = search == .played ? "in the played windows" : "in the whole files"
187	   187	            var items = moves.enumerated().map { index, move in
188	   188	                seconds(move.delta) + " ("
189	   189	                    + (index == 0 ? "confidence " : "") + String(format: "%.2f", move.confidence)
190	   190	                    + ")"
191	   191	            }
192	   192	            let last = items.removeLast()

197	   197	            / Double(ReelTime.perSecond)

199	   199	            + ". A match applies on its own at confidence ≥ "

201	   201	            + String(format: "%g", AudioSyncMatch.confidentMargin)
202	   202	            + " above the next candidate; one ≥ " + String(format: "%g", AudioSyncMatch.plausibleZ)
203	   203	            + " within " + String(format: "%.0f", radius) + " s of where clip \(mover) sits now "

321	    67	                + ", confidence " + String(format: "%.2f", row.confidence)

325	    71	            + (weak.count == 1 ? "it" : "them") + ", once the person has agreed to "

361	     3	/// Synchronize Audio's drift correction (road map "audio-sync", AS-2; spec
362	     4	/// §11 SY-6, SY-8..SY-10): whether a measured drift is corrected, the rate
363	     5	/// band a clip is matched within, where the corrected mover goes, how long
364	     6	/// it becomes and in which order its two ops run.
365	     7	///
366	     8	/// Pure, as `AudioSync.plan` is: readings and a fitted line in, a speed, a
367	     9	/// delta and ops out. The correction is the existing `set_speed` op with
368	    10	/// `keep_pitch: false` (SY-6): the model keeps the rate as an f64, the plan
369	    11	/// plays it as integer ticks over integer ticks, and `.varispeed` resamples
370	    12	/// it with none of the time-pitch algorithm's processing.
371	    13	extension AudioSync {
372	    14	
373	    15	    // MARK: - The numbers (SY-8, SY-9)
374	    16	
375	    17	    /// 0.2%: the furthest from ×1 a clip may play and still be matched, and
376	    18	    /// the furthest a correction may take it.
377	    19	    static let maximumRateDeviation = 0.002
378	    20	    /// A drift under this, over the whole overlap, is left alone.
379	    21	    static let minimumCorrectionMilliseconds = 5.0
380	    22	    /// A drift must be at least this many times its own uncertainty to be
381	    23	    /// corrected — the significance test (the owner's choice, 2026-10-15).
382	    24	    static let minimumSignificance = 3.0
383	    25	
384	    26	    /// What becomes of one mover's drift: a new speed, or left as it is
385	    27	    /// with the sentence that says why (nil when it was not measured, whose
386	    28	    /// own note says why).
387	    29	    enum Correction: Equatable {
388	    30	        case apply(speed: Double)
389	    31	        case leave(note: String?)
390	    32	    }
391	    33	
392	    34	    // MARK: - Deciding (SY-8)
393	    35	
394	    36	    /// The correction for `drift` measured on a clip playing at `speed`, the
395	    37	    /// three rules in SY-8's order: corrected when `|drift_ms| ≥ max(5, 3 ×
396	    38	    /// drift_error_ms)` and the new speed stays in SY-9's band. The
397	    39	    /// uncertainty is a test of significance, not a cap.
398	    40	    static func correction(for drift: AudioSyncMatch.DriftAnswer, speed: Double) -> Correction {
399	    41	        guard case .measured(let fit) = drift else { return .leave(note: nil) }
400	    42	        if abs(fit.milliseconds) < minimumCorrectionMilliseconds {
401	    43	            return .leave(
402	    44	                note: "a drift of " + String(format: "%.2f", fit.milliseconds)
403	    45	                    + " ms over the overlap is under the "
404	    46	                    + "\(String(format: "%g", minimumCorrectionMilliseconds)) ms Synchronize "
405	    47	                    + "Audio corrects.")
406	    48	        }
407	    49	        if abs(fit.milliseconds) < minimumSignificance * fit.errorMilliseconds {
408	    50	            return .leave(
409	    51	                note: "a drift of " + String(format: "%.2f", fit.milliseconds)
410	    52	                    + " ms over the overlap is under "
411	    53	                    + "\(String(format: "%g", minimumSignificance)) times its uncertainty (±"
412	    54	                    + String(format: "%.2f", fit.errorMilliseconds) + " ms), so it cannot be "
413	    55	                    + "told from no drift.")
414	    56	        }
415	    57	        let corrected = speed * (1 - fit.rate)
416	    58	        guard inBand(corrected) else {
417	    59	            return .leave(
418	    60	                note: "correcting it would play the clip at ×" + String(format: "%g", corrected)
419	    61	                    + ", beyond the 0.2% Synchronize Audio corrects.")
420	    62	        }
421	    63	        return .apply(speed: corrected)
422	    64	    }
423	    65	
424	    66	    // MARK: - The band (SY-9)
425	    67	
426	    68	    /// Why a clip playing at `rate` cannot be matched; nil within the band.
427	    69	    static func rateProblem(_ rate: Double) -> String? {
428	    70	        guard !inBand(rate) else { return nil }
429	    71	        return "plays at ×\(String(format: "%g", rate)); Synchronize Audio lines up clips "
430	    72	            + "playing at ×1 or within 0.2% of it."
431	    73	    }
432	    74	
433	    75	    /// Why a clip whose speed is ×1 but whose source is stretched to `rate`
434	    76	    /// cannot be matched, even inside the band: its speed is not its rate.
435	    77	    static func stretched(_ rate: Double) -> String {
436	    78	        "plays at ×\(String(format: "%g", rate)) though its speed is ×1; Synchronize Audio "
437	    79	            + "lines up clips whose speed is the rate they play at."
438	    80	    }
439	    81	
440	    82	    /// Why a RAMPED clip, mover or anchor, cannot be matched (spec §11
441	    83	    /// SR-20 (e)): the drift line assumes one rate over the clip.
442	    84	    static let ramped = "ramps its speed (a speed action changes its rate over its length); "
443	    85	        + "Synchronize Audio lines up clips playing at one rate."
444	    86	
445	    87	    /// `|rate − 1| ≤ maximumRateDeviation`, as a closed range so that the
446	    88	    /// band's own edges (×1.002, ×0.998) are inside it in binary arithmetic.
447	    89	    private static func inBand(_ rate: Double) -> Bool {
448	    90	        ((1 - maximumRateDeviation)...(1 + maximumRateDeviation)).contains(rate)
449	    91	    }
450	    92	
451	    93	    // MARK: - The corrected span (SY-6, SY-10)
452	    94	
453	    95	    /// The duration `set_speed` writes when a clip of `duration` playing at
454	    96	    /// `old` is set to `new`: its content `round(d·old)` over `new`, snapped
455	    97	    /// to the grid and at least one frame — the core's arithmetic without its
456	    98	    /// hold to the file, which stays the core's backstop.
457	    99	    static func durationAtSpeed(_ duration: Ticks, from old: Double, to new: Double, fps: Fps)
458	   100	        -> Ticks {
459	   101	        let content = (Double(duration) * old).rounded()
460	   102	        let scaled = ReelTime.snapToFrame(Ticks((content / new).rounded()), fps: fps)
461	   103	        return max(scaled, fps.frameDuration)
462	   104	    }
463	   105	
464	   106	    /// The move that puts a mover set to `speed` in sync along the fitted
465	   107	    /// line (SY-6): `set_speed` keeps its start S and in point I, so source
466	   108	    /// tick μ plays at `S + δ + (μ − I)/s'`, which is where the anchor plays
467	   109	    /// the same sound when `δ = zeroA + 75·c/(1 − ρ) − S + I/s'` (c in
468	   110	    /// samples, 75 ticks each, SY-21); snapped.
469	   111	    static func correctedDelta(
470	   112	        anchor: Reading, mover: Reading, drift: AudioSyncMatch.Drift, speed: Double, fps: Fps
471	   113	    ) -> Ticks {
472	   114	        let shift = Double(AudioSyncPHAT.sampleTicks) * drift.intercept / (1 - drift.rate)
473	   115	        let exact = Double(anchor.zero) + shift - Double(mover.start)
474	   116	            + Double(mover.sourceIn) / speed
475	   117	        return ReelTime.snapToFrame(Ticks(exact.rounded()), fps: fps)
476	   118	    }
477	   119	
478	   120	    /// One mover's ops, each only when it changes something, ordered so
479	   121	    /// that every span in between lies inside the old one or the final one
480	   122	    /// (SY-10): a mover that grows moves first, one that shrinks or keeps
481	   123	    /// its length changes speed first. A mover trimmed at its head (SY-16,
482	   124	    /// `trimTo` the `trim_start` target S + e) changes speed first, so the
483	   125	    /// trim advances its in point at the new speed, then trims, then moves.
484	   126	    static func ops(
485	   127	        clip: UInt32, delta: Ticks, from old: Double, to new: Double?, duration: Ticks,
486	   128	        newDuration: Ticks, trimTo: Ticks? = nil
487	   129	    ) -> [ReelOp] {
488	   130	        let move: ReelOp? = delta != 0 ? ReelOp.moveClip(clips: [clip], delta: delta) : nil
489	   131	        var speed: ReelOp?
490	   132	        if let new = new, new != old {
491	   133	            speed = ReelOp.setSpeed(clip: clip, rate: new, keepPitch: false)
492	   134	        }
493	   135	        if let trimTo {
494	   136	            return [speed, ReelOp.trimStart(clip: clip, to: trimTo), move].compactMap { $0 }
495	   137	        }
496	   138	        if newDuration > duration {
497	   139	            return [move, speed].compactMap { $0 }
498	   140	        }
499	   141	        return [speed, move].compactMap { $0 }
500	   142	    }
501	   143	}

504	     3	/// Where Synchronize Audio's one GCC-PHAT refinement runs (#302; spec §11
505	     4	/// SY-32, amending SY-20's and SY-29's centred region): moved out of
506	     5	/// `AudioSync.swift`, where the region was the overlap's centre 30 s.
507	     6	///
508	     7	/// It is pure, as `plan` is: an overlap, the two readings' timeline-grid
509	     8	/// features and masks and the line in, a range of anchor timeline samples
510	     9	/// out. It only chooses WHERE: the refinement, its z and the gate are
511	    10	/// `AudioSyncPHAT`'s and `plan`'s (SY-29), and there is still one region.
512	    11	extension AudioSync {
513	    12	
514	    13	    /// SY-32's region: `overlap` (anchor timeline frames) ×128, in anchor
515	    14	    /// timeline samples, when it holds at most W = `maximumRegionSamples /
516	    15	    /// hop` frames; else the W frames whose features agree most along
517	    16	    /// `line`. Frame f scores `Σ_k A[f, k]·M[m(f), k]`, A and M the features
518	    17	    /// `standardised` as the match was (over the speech frames when it
519	    18	    /// matched on speech), `m(f) = f − round((c + ρ·128f)/128)`, and 0 when
520	    19	    /// f or m(f) lies outside its file. The start s in `[lo, hi − W]` with
521	    20	    /// the greatest summed score wins; the centred start `⌊(lo + hi)/2⌋ −
522	    21	    /// ⌊W/2⌋` is the first candidate, replaced only by a strictly greater
523	    22	    /// sum or an equal one nearer it.
524	    23	    static func refinementRegion(
525	    24	        overlap: Range<Int>, anchorFrames: [Float], moverFrames: [Float], anchorSpeech: [Bool]?,
526	    25	        moverSpeech: [Bool]?, matchedOn: AudioSyncMatch.MatchedOn, line: AudioSyncPHAT.Line
527	    26	    ) -> Range<Int> {
528	    27	        let hop = SyncFeatures.hop
529	    28	        let span = AudioSyncPHAT.maximumRegionSamples / hop
530	    29	        let lo = overlap.lowerBound
531	    30	        let hi = overlap.upperBound
532	    31	        guard overlap.count > span else { return (lo * hop)..<(hi * hop) }
533	    32	
534	    33	        let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
535	    34	        let onSpeech = matchedOn == .speech
536	    35	        let a = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(anchorFrames, speech: onSpeech ? anchorSpeech : nil)
537	    36	        let m = AudioSyncMatch.standardised(moverFrames, speech: onSpeech ? moverSpeech : nil)
538	    37	        let anchorCount = a.count / width
539	    38	        let moverCount = m.count / width
540	    39	
541	    40	        // prefix[i] = Σ score over the overlap's first i frames.
542	    41	        var prefix = [Double](repeating: 0, count: overlap.count + 1)
543	    42	        a.withUnsafeBufferPointer { anchor in
544	    43	            m.withUnsafeBufferPointer { mover in
545	    44	                for (index, f) in overlap.enumerated() {
546	    45	                    let lag = ((line.intercept + line.rate * Double(f * hop)) / Double(hop))
547	    46	                        .rounded()
548	    47	                    let g = f - Int(lag)
549	    48	                    var score = 0.0
550	    49	                    if f >= 0, f < anchorCount, g >= 0, g < moverCount {
551	    50	                        let x = f * width
552	    51	                        let y = g * width
553	    52	                        for k in 0..<width { score += Double(anchor[x + k]) * Double(mover[y + k]) }
554	    53	                    }
555	    54	                    prefix[index + 1] = prefix[index] + score
556	    55	                }
557	    56	            }
558	    57	        }
559	    58	        func sum(_ start: Int) -> Double { prefix[start - lo + span] - prefix[start - lo] }
560	    59	
561	    60	        let last = hi - span
562	    61	        let centred = min(max(lo, (lo + hi) / 2 - span / 2), last)
563	    62	        var best = centred
564	    63	        var bestSum = sum(centred)
565	    64	        for start in lo...last {
566	    65	            let value = sum(start)
567	    66	            if value > bestSum || (value == bestSum && abs(start - centred) < abs(best - centred)) {
568	    67	                best = start
569	    68	                bestSum = value
570	    69	            }
571	    70	        }
572	    71	        return (best * hop)..<((best + span) * hop)
573	    72	    }
574	    73	}

1	import Accelerate
     2	import Foundation
     3	
     4	/// Synchronize Audio's signal arithmetic (road maps "audio-sync" and
     5	/// "audio-sync-2"; spec §11 SY-12..SY-14, SY-17, SY-18, SY-21): two files'
     6	/// cached features (and, when both hold speech, their speech masks) in,
     7	/// candidate lags and their confidence out.
     8	///
     9	/// It is pure — no AppKit, no document, no disk. `AudioSync.read` hands it
    10	/// each file's `cache/sync/<media id>.bin` frames (`SyncFeatures`: 26 MFCCs
    11	/// per 16 ms of SOURCE time), and `AudioSync.find` and `plan` turn what it
    12	/// answers into ops or a refusal.
    13	///
    14	/// **The coarse match is on FEATURES** (SY-12). Each stretch compared is
    15	/// standardised per coefficient — gain, microphone and room move a
    16	/// coefficient's level and spread, which standardising takes off — and the
    17	/// correlation is the SUM over coefficients of their full cross-correlations,
    18	/// `c(L) = Σ_k Σ_m x_k[m + L]·y_k[m]`, one zero-padded FFT per coefficient and
    19	/// one inverse of the summed cross-spectrum. A lag's confidence is its
    20	/// z-score against every lag (BBC's `audio-offset-finder`, as `mfccsync.py`
    21	/// measured it on the owner's files). `search` answers the candidates and the
    22	/// best peak near where the mover already sits; `AudioSync+Search.swift`
    23	/// chooses between them (SY-14, SY-18).
    24	///
    25	/// **Speech only** (SY-17): when both stretches hold `minimumSpeechFrames`
    26	/// frames the cached Silero VAD calls speech, each is standardised over its
    27	/// own speech frames and every other frame is 0, so only frames that are
    28	/// speech in both correlate; otherwise every frame counts, as above.
    29	///
    30	/// **Drift** runs on the same features (SY-21): each of its windows is one
    31	/// `search` with a narrower `radius`, the line through them fitted in
    32	/// `AudioSyncDrift.swift`, and each window refined on the samples by
    33	/// `AudioSyncPHAT.swift` (SY-20), which shares `refine` from here.
    34	enum AudioSyncMatch {
    35	
    36	    // MARK: - The numbers (SY-12..SY-14)
    37	
    38	    /// 2 s of frames: a played window under it is not searched, and a file
    39	    /// under it is too short to match.
    40	    static let minimumStretchFrames = 125
    41	    /// A lag overlapping fewer frames (or the shorter stretch, when that is
    42	    /// shorter) may not be a candidate; it still counts in z's mean and sd.
    43	    static let minimumOverlapFrames = 125
    44	    /// 0.96 s: how far apart two candidates must be — a peak's own shoulders
    45	    /// are not a second candidate.
    46	    static let exclusionFrames = 60
    47	    /// The most candidates a search answers.
    48	    static let candidateCount = 4
    49	    /// The z a best candidate needs to be chosen on its own — the CONFIDENT
    50	    /// tier, which applies without asking (SY-18; BBC's `audio-offset-finder`
    51	    /// reads "> 10 trustworthy"), and applied only when GCC-PHAT confirms it
    52	    /// (SY-29).
    53	    static let confidentZ = 10.0
    54	    /// How far, in z, it must stand above the second candidate.
    55	    static let confidentMargin = 1.5
    56	    /// The z the peak near the mover's placement needs to be chosen — the
    57	    /// WEAK tier, which is asked about, never applied silently (SY-18), and
    58	    /// offered only when GCC-PHAT confirms it (SY-29).
    59	    static let plausibleZ = 4.0
    60	    /// 3.008 s: how near the mover's current placement that peak must lie.
    61	    static let placementRadiusFrames = 188
    62	    /// The VAD probability at or above which a frame is speech (SY-17):
    63	    /// Silero's default, and `detect_silence`'s default `voice_confidence`.
    64	    static let speechProbability: Float = 0.5
    65	    /// The speech frames each stretch needs for a speech-only search (2 s).
    66	    static let minimumSpeechFrames = 125
    67	
    68	    /// A feature frame's centre after its start: half of `fftSize` at
    69	    /// `sampleRate` — exactly 19,200 ticks, written as the division for
    70	    /// `SyncFeatures.frameTicks`' reason.
    71	    static var frameCentreTicks: Ticks {
    72	        ReelTime.perSecond * Ticks(SyncFeatures.fftSize / 2) / Ticks(SyncFeatures.sampleRate)
    73	    }
    74	
    75	    /// What a search correlated (SY-17).
    76	    enum MatchedOn: String {
    77	        case speech, sound
    78	    }
    79	
    80	    // MARK: - The feature search (SY-12, SY-14)
    81	
    82	    /// One candidate lag: the anchor's frame minus the mover's frame of the
    83	    /// same sound, file-relative on the timeline grid and refined, with its
    84	    /// z-score.
    85	    struct Candidate: Equatable {
    86	        let lag: Double
    87	        let z: Double
    88	    }
    89	
    90	    /// What one search found: its candidates, highest first, and the highest
    91	    /// peak near where the mover already sits (nil when there is none).
    92	    struct SearchResult: Equatable {
    93	        let candidates: [Candidate]
    94	        let nearPlacement: Candidate?
    95	        var matchedOn: MatchedOn = .sound
    96	    }
    97	
    98	    // MARK: - Speech masks (SY-17)
    99	
   100	    /// Which of a file's `frames` feature frames are speech: frame f is when
   101	    /// the probability of the chunk holding its centre, chunk
   102	    /// `(f·frameTicks + frameCentreTicks) / chunkTicks` (the last when past
   103	    /// the end), is at least `speechProbability`. All false with no
   104	    /// probabilities.
   105	    static func speechMask(_ probabilities: [Float], frames: Int) -> [Bool] {
   106	        guard !probabilities.isEmpty else { return [Bool](repeating: false, count: frames) }
   107	        let chunk = MediaSpeech.chunkTicks
   108	        return (0..<frames).map { f in
   109	            let index = min(
   110	                Int((Ticks(f) * SyncFeatures.frameTicks + frameCentreTicks) / chunk),
   111	                probabilities.count - 1)
   112	            return probabilities[index] >= speechProbability
   113	        }
   114	    }
   115	
   116	    /// `mask` on the timeline grid of a clip playing at `speed`, as
   117	    /// `resampledFrames` takes its frames: frame k is source frame
   118	    /// `round(k·speed)` (the last when past it). The mask itself at ×1.
   119	    static func resampledMask(_ mask: [Bool], speed: Double) -> [Bool] {
   120	        let count = mask.count
   121	        guard speed != 1, speed.isFinite, speed > 0, count > 1 else { return mask }
   122	        let last = count - 1
   123	        let resampledCount = Int((Double(last) / speed).rounded(.down)) + 1
   124	        return (0..<resampledCount).map { mask[min(Int((Double($0) * speed).rounded()), last)] }
   125	    }
   126	
   127	    /// `frames` standardised per coefficient: mean 0, sd 1 (the population
   128	    /// sd), over the whole stretch, or with `speech` over its true frames
   129	    /// only, every false frame then 0 (SY-17). A coefficient whose sd is
   130	    /// under 1e-6 is 0.
   131	    static func standardised(_ frames: [Float], speech: [Bool]? = nil) -> [Float] {
   132	        let width = SyncFeatures.coefficients
   133	        let count = frames.count / width
   134	        var result = [Float](repeating: 0, count: count * width)
   135	        guard count > 0 else { return result }
   136	        let counted = speech.map { mask in (0..<count).filter { $0 < mask.count && mask[$0] } }

190	   190	    /// Which points are inliers about the Theil–Sen line: its slope b the
191	   191	    /// median of `(yⱼ − yᵢ)/(xⱼ − xᵢ)` over every pair with xⱼ ≠ xᵢ, its
192	   192	    /// intercept the median of `y − b·x`; a point is in when its residual is
193	   193	    /// at most `max(driftInlierScale·1.4826·MAD, driftInlierFloorSamples)`,
194	   194	    /// MAD the median absolute residual. Every point with fewer than 2, or no
195	   195	    /// pair to take a slope of.
196	   196	    private static func inliers(_ xs: [Double], _ ys: [Double]) -> [Bool] {
197	   197	        func median(_ values: [Double]) -> Double {
198	   198	            let sorted = values.sorted()
199	   199	            let middle = sorted.count / 2
200	   200	            return sorted.count % 2 == 1 ? sorted[middle] : (sorted[middle - 1] + sorted[middle]) / 2
201	   201	        }
202	   202	        var slopes: [Double] = []
203	   203	        for i in xs.indices {
204	   204	            for j in xs.indices where j > i && xs[j] != xs[i] {
205	   205	                slopes.append((ys[j] - ys[i]) / (xs[j] - xs[i]))
206	   206	            }
207	   207	        }
208	   208	        guard xs.count >= 2, !slopes.isEmpty else { return [Bool](repeating: true, count: xs.count) }

210	   210	        let a = median(zip(xs, ys).map { $1 - b * $0 })
211	   211	        let r = zip(xs, ys).map { $1 - a - b * $0 }
212	   212	        let threshold = max(
213	   213	            driftInlierScale * 1.4826 * median(r.map { abs($0) }), driftInlierFloorSamples)

217	   217	    /// The ordinary least-squares line through (`xs`, `ys`), in samples, as a
218	   218	    /// `Drift` over an overlap of `length` frames cut every `step` frames.
219	   219	    private static func line(
220	   220	        _ xs: [Double], _ ys: [Double], length: Int, step: Int, on source: DriftSource
221	   221	    ) -> Drift {
222	   222	        let count = Double(xs.count)
223	   223	        let meanX = xs.reduce(0, +) / count
224	   224	        let meanY = ys.reduce(0, +) / count
225	   225	        var sxx = 0.0
226	   226	        var sxy = 0.0
227	   227	        for (x, y) in zip(xs, ys) {
228	   228	            sxx += (x - meanX) * (x - meanX)
229	   229	            sxy += (x - meanX) * (y - meanY)
230	   230	        }
231	   231	        let rate = sxy / sxx
232	   232	        let intercept = meanY - rate * meanX
233	   233	        var squares = 0.0
234	   234	        for (x, y) in zip(xs, ys) {
235	   235	            let residual = y - intercept - rate * x
236	   236	            squares += residual * residual
237	   237	        }
238	   238	        let standardError = (squares / (count - 2) / sxx).squareRoot()

240	   240	            ? (Double(driftWindowFrames) / Double(step)).squareRoot() : 1

243	   243	            / (Double(SyncFeatures.sampleRate) / 1000)

245	   245	            ppm: rate * 1e6, milliseconds: rate * overlapMilliseconds, rate: rate,
246	   246	            intercept: intercept, errorMilliseconds: standardError * widened * overlapMilliseconds,
247	   247	            windows: xs.count, on: source)

37:## Tape pitch is rendered in the background
38-
39-With Keep pitch off, at any rate but ×1 and up to ×12, Frame Job renders the clip's sound in the background before it plays. The clip is silent in the preview until that finishes. When it's ready, the sound plays at that speed's tape pitch, exactly in step with the picture.
40-
41-- Renders run one at a time, and the wait grows with the clip's length and rate.
42-- A change to the clip's timing, such as a new rate, a trim or a split, starts a new render.

content.content:
493:When a clip plays faster or slower, its sound either keeps its pitch or changes pitch like tape. The **Keep pitch** checkbox is in the Speed section of the Clip sub-tab and is on by default. Above ×12 a clip's audio is left out of the mix. See [Speed](speed.md) for speed changes, speed ramps and how their audio is rendered.
576:*Agents:* `set_track` with `compressor: {threshold_db, ratio, attack, release, makeup_db}` (attack and release in ticks) and `limiter: {ceiling_db, release}`. Each object replaces the whole setting (a key left out takes its default) and `null` turns it off. Refused inside a `scope`.
643:- **It corrects drift.** If two clocks run at slightly different rates, the recorder slowly falls out of sync over a long take. When the clips overlap for at least 60 seconds, Frame Job measures that drift and corrects it by playing the clip at a slightly different speed, at most 0.2 % from ×1. The correction is a plain resample, so the pitch moves very slightly with it. Drift is left alone when it is under 5 ms over the overlap, when it is too small to tell from no drift (under three times its own uncertainty), or when the speed it needs is more than 0.2 % from ×1. The corrected speed appears in the clip's Speed section (for example ×1.0004), with Keep pitch turned off. The command shows no drift figure of its own; that speed is where the correction shows. Like any clip at a speed other than ×1 with Keep pitch off, the corrected clip's sound is rendered in the background, so it is briefly silent in the preview after the correction, and again after each trim, split or speed change of it (see [Speed](speed.md)); an export waits for it.
661:> Weak match: play “record.aifc” at ×1.0004, correcting its drift?

A match is **weak** when no candidate is confident, but the best one within about 3 seconds of where the clip already sits has a confidence of at least 4. Because a weak match might be unrelated sound, it is never applied without asking. A **Weak match** sheet appears, for example:

> Weak match: move “record.aifc” 0.80 s earlier (trimming 0.80 s off its head)?

A clip that doesn't need to move, only to have its drift corrected, is asked about this way instead:

> Weak match: play “record.aifc” at ×1.0004, correcting its drift?

When several clips are weak, one sheet lists them all, separated by semicolons.

Under the question, the sheet gives the anchor's name, each match's confidence and the rule the match fell short of. **Apply** (the default button) makes every listed change as one undo step. **Cancel** leaves everything as it is.

When nothing matches, the command is refused. The refusal names the offsets it did find and their confidences, so you can move the clip near the right one and try again.

### When it refuses

From the menu, clips in the selection that play no sound (a still, a file with no audio track, a clip with its audio switched off) and nests are left out without a message, and the command needs at least two other clips with sound. To synchronize clips inside a nest, open it (⌘↓) and select them there.

Synchronize Audio is all or nothing. If any clip can't be matched, nothing moves. Frame Job beeps and lists every reason at the foot of the inspector. A clip can't be synchronized when it:

- has no sound to line up by (its analysis found no sound at all)
- is still being analysed. Its sound features or speech haven't been written yet, so try again in a moment.
- holds under 2 seconds of sound
- plays more than 0.2 % away from ×1
- plays at a rate other than its speed setting
- plays reversed
- ramps its speed (a speed action changes its rate over its length)
- would share a track with another clip being synchronized
- would never play at the same time as the anchor once lined up
- matches the anchor's sound, but the waveforms don't line up there (for example two takes of the same words), so they are not one recording
- matches the anchor's sound, but the two share less than 2 seconds of waveform there, too little to confirm it is one recording
- would overlap another clip on its own track after the move
- would lose so much of its head that less than a frame is left

If the clips are already in sync, nothing changes and Frame Job beeps. The menu item is enabled only when at least two selected clips that aren't nests can play sound.
